title: Reflowing Zoom, Hugged Wraps, Fitted Type, Background Borders & Honest Checkboxes
description: Five techniques that hand a measurement back to the browser instead of computing it in JavaScript.

drops.title: Zoom That Reflows
drops.description: Chrome 150 made zoom animatable — and zoom, unlike transform, is a layout the engine believes in.
drops.concept: Three parallel tracks scale the same card with zoom, transform: scale() and font-size. Only zoom feeds back into layout, so its neighbours get pushed along and its text re-wraps, while the transform silently overlaps them. Live readouts report layout width, line count and the neighbour's offset so the difference is measurable, not just visible.

interaction.mouse: Drag the scale and duration sliders to set the target and timing.
interaction.click: Animate runs all three tracks together; Reset returns them to 1.0.
interaction.touch: Sliders and buttons are tap-sized; the panel stacks above the demo on narrow screens.

drops.title: Hug the Wrap
drops.description: A box that shrinks to its longest wrapped line, measured entirely in CSS with anchors and view timelines.
drops.concept: Wrapped text normally stretches its box to the full container, leaving dead space beside the ragged edge. Komarov's shrinkwrap anchors an invisible probe to the inline content, gives it a view timeline, and animates two registered number properties across a 10000px range; their difference is the real content width, fed straight back into inline-size. Chat bubbles, tags and a headline all hug their text, with a toggle to switch the technique off and a probe overlay to see the ruler.

interaction.mouse: Slide the max inline-size and text length; the measured width and the dead space saved update live.
interaction.click: Toggle the technique off to compare, or reveal the anchored probe doing the measuring.
interaction.touch: Controls stack above the rails; every bubble re-measures on resize.

drops.title: Type Measured to the Box
drops.description: text-fit asks the layout engine for the font size that fills the space, instead of clamp() and guesswork.
drops.concept: A poster headline, a grid of wildly uneven names and a side-by-side against fixed-size-plus-ellipsis. Each element declares that it should fill its box; where the browser lacks text-fit, a nine-step binary search resolves the same intent so the behaviour is visible either way, and the panel reports which path is running.

interaction.mouse: Drag poster width and the size range; type into the headline field to re-fit everything.
interaction.click: Focus the textarea to replace the sample headline across all three demos.
interaction.touch: The panel moves inline above the demos and all controls stay reachable.

drops.title: Borders From the Background
drops.description: background-clip: border-area turns one ordinary background into a gradient border, corners intact.
drops.concept: Gradient borders have meant a doubled pseudo-element, a masked wrapper, or border-image at the cost of border-radius. Clipping a conic gradient to the border area needs neither. Six cards and five pills animate a registered angle property on hover only, so a page full of them costs nothing at rest; without the new value the demo falls back to border-image and you can watch the corners square off.

interaction.mouse: Hover a card or pill to start its sweep; sliders set border width, spin period and radius.
interaction.click: Pills are real buttons with visible focus rings.
interaction.touch: Tapping a card starts its animation; the always-running row shows the full sweep without hover.

drops.title: A Checkbox Worth Keeping
drops.description: A styled checkbox that never stops being a native input — the honest pattern until ::checkmark exists.
drops.concept: The real input is stretched invisibly across the visible box, so focus, keyboard, form submission and the accessibility tree are untouched, and an SVG tick is revealed by :checked. A live fieldset reports its own values, a narrowing column shows baseline alignment holding as labels wrap to three lines, and radios plus an indeterminate state come from the same box scaled by a single font-size.

interaction.mouse: Click any label or box to toggle; the readout lists the checked values.
interaction.click: Tab through the group — the focus ring is the input's own, matched to the box radius.
interaction.touch: The whole label is the hit target; sliders rescale every control from one font-size.
